chunks: From him, from Yasser the servant, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

The one who removes himself from singing, then in Paradise there is a tree which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands the winds to stir, so a sound is heard for it the likes of which have not been heard, and the one who does not remove himself from it, will not hear it.

key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the abode of eternal bliss
key_terms.الْغِنَاءِ: Singing or music, specifically melodic vocal or instrumental performance
key_terms.شَجَرَةً: A tree, specifically a unique tree in Paradise mentioned in this context
key_terms.صَوْتاً: A sound, specifically the unique divine sound produced by the tree

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for abstaining from singing in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) linking the spiritual discipline of abstaining from *al-ghina'* (melodic singing) to a specific sensory reward in Paradise. The hadith posits a unique tree whose rustling produces a sound unparalleled in creation, accessible only to those who purify themselves from this specific form of vocal music, reflecting the Shia emphasis on auditory purity as a component of spiritual refinement.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Yasser the servant, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who removes himself from the singing (music), so in the Paradise there is a tree which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Commands the winds that they should stir it, so such sounds are heard for it the likes of which have not been heard, and the one who does not remove himself from it, would not hear it’.
en.sarwar: 19. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Yasir al-Khadim who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If one keeps his soul clean of al-Ghina’ (music (and singing)), Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, commands the winds to move a tree in the garden (paradises). From this tree a sound is heard the like of which is never heard, and those who fail to keep their souls clean of al-Ghina’ (music (and singing)) will not be able to hear it.’”
